notes:
I couldn't do the research this time, so I have no verse-by-verse notes for Isaiah 49 to give you.

I asked for six pages at once: Enduring Word's Isaiah 49 page, the Precept Austin commentary, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, and the NET Bible notes. Some replies came back, but my code broke while reading them, so I never saw what any page said. After that the tool wouldn't let me run any more searches or page fetches in this turn, so I couldn't try again.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything for any verse; any notes I gave you now would have no real source behind them.

If you ask again, I'll start over and work through:
1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** each tradition's own sites. Likely key verses are v. 3 (why the Servant is called "Israel"), v. 6 (a light for the nations), v. 8 (Paul quotes this in 2 Corinthians 6:2), v. 16 (inscribed on God's palms) and vv. 22–26 (how the promises to Zion are fulfilled).
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings; and any popular modern teaching on these verses that the allowed sites discuss.

Each point will be written verse by verse in my own words, with its URL.
